prompt.brief: Design a collaborative document platform like Notion or Google Docs with real-time editing, sharing, comments, search, version history, and offline recovery.
successSignals: Model document operations as an ordered, durable log and derive snapshots, search indexes, comments, and notifications.
Use a CRDT or operational-transform protocol for concurrent edits, with reconnect cursors and bounded document history.
Separate document permissions from cached collaboration presence and ensure revoked users cannot read future updates.
Explain offline edits, conflict resolution, snapshots, compaction, sharing, export, deletion, and audit history.

functional: Create folders and documents, edit rich content concurrently, comment, mention collaborators, search, and share by role.
Stream remote operations, acknowledge client sequence numbers, show presence, and restore from a version or snapshot.
Support offline edits, export, retention, legal deletion, link revocation, and per-operation audit records.
nonFunctional: Target p95 operation acknowledgement below 150 ms for a connected document and reconcile offline edits on reconnect.
Scale millions of documents by document and tenant while isolating very large or highly collaborative documents.
Never lose an accepted operation; deduplicate client sequence numbers and preserve a replayable operation log.
Degrade to local editing and queued sync when collaboration, search, or notification services are unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Support 50 million documents, 1 million daily editors, and up to 1,000 concurrent collaborators on a hot document.
Partition by tenant and document ID; shard hot operation streams and snapshot large documents separately.
Retain encrypted operation logs and periodic snapshots while compacting obsolete history under retention policy.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Collaborative document platform like Notion or G commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Collaborative document platform like Notion or G writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Collaborative document platform like Notion or G version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Collaborative document platform like Notion or G by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Collaborative document platform like Notion or G work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Collaborative document platform like Notion or G projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Collaborative document platform like Notion or G projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
